causal_chain: archiveLoop spawns storage-ark-export.py on the same ark.db while produceArk POSTs /t5/ark/state
ArkStore sets PRAGMA busy_timeout=15 and accept takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE
node:sqlite busy failure is Error code ERR_SQLITE_ERROR errcode 5 message database is locked
routes.ts rethrows that message; onError maps it and every other unexpected error to HTTP 503 ark_dependency_unavailable
export sqlite timeout is 100ms plus a 1s SQLITE_BUSY retry budget, so the export transaction can commit after accept already failed
finish() calls batch_payload() while BEGIN IMMEDIATE is held; spool fsync/rename/sha in publish_prepared run before the following one-statement transaction

same_body_also_covers: statfsSync throw from archivePolicy before BEGIN

idempotency.effect: duplicate, original received_at_ms, no second outbox row
idempotency.client: produceArk asserts 200 and does not retry

reviewer_host_busy_probe.note: Export tests already require Linux for real busy deadlines. Configured 15 is not this host's wall clock, and 2086ms matches neither 15ms nor this ~550ms probe.

minimal_fix.change: In finish(), compare envelopes before BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Inside the transaction check only COUNT(*), MIN(id), MAX(id), SUM(bytes), then DELETE/UPDATE.
minimal_fix.residual: claim() of up to 1000 updates and every COMMIT wal fsync can still exceed the peer busy wait if the db volume is slow

Linux: block inside finish() while BEGIN IMMEDIATE is held; HTTP 503 ark_dependency_unavailable AND errcode 5 AND code ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
Control: throw new Error('forced_non_busy') yields the same HTTP body and must not satisfy errcode===5; a 503-only assertion fails the test
After the holder releases, the same snapshot commits once: accepted if the busy attempt did not commit, duplicate with unchanged received_at_ms and no extra outbox row if it did
